reason: The passage contains no statement or implication that the elite are inherently better than regular people. The text addresses the entire people (העם) collectively and uniformly in God's provision of manna. All individuals are instructed to gather equally for their needs, and the Sabbath is presented as a provision granted to the entire community equally. The test presented (obedience to God's commandments) applies uniformly to all people without distinction of status or class. When some individuals disobeyed by gathering on the seventh day, the issue was their failure to follow the divine command—not a judgment about their social position. The passage emphasizes collective obedience and equal treatment under God's law, not any inherent superiority of an elite class.
